title: A High-Throughput Private Inference Engine Based on 3D Stacked Memory
problem: Existing FHE-based inference architectures suffer from a memory access bottleneck that severely limits throughput when performing homomorphic operations on encrypted neural network data. The bandwidth-limited memory systems cannot efficiently support the massive data movement required for FHE polynomial operations.
motivation: Private inference using FHE enables neural network inference directly on encrypted data without decryption, critical for privacy-preserving machine learning applications across sensitive domains.
method: H3 solves the memory bottleneck by physically stacking memory chips directly on top of the computing chip using 3D hybrid bonding, so data travels a much shorter distance. It adjusts how it breaks down the polynomial calculations (the complex math operations encrypted data requires) on the fly, decomposing them dynamically to minimize data movement. An efficient broadcast mechanism routes the encrypted data directly to the processing arrays that need it, significantly reducing memory traffic and delays.
key_novelty: H3 stacks memory chips on top of the processor die using 3D hybrid bonding and dynamically decomposes polynomial calculations to eliminate the memory bottleneck that limits encrypted neural network inference.
contributions: Hardware-software co-design enabling dynamic polynomial decomposition adjustment for FHE operations
3D hybrid bonding architecture integrating logic die with multi-layer embedded DRAM
Efficient broadcast mechanism for optimized data routing to processing units
52% throughput improvement over 7nm FHE accelerators with compact 192mm² footprint
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; scalability to larger neural networks beyond ResNet-20, power consumption, and memory density trade-offs are not addressed.
primary_theme: 3D memory integration for FHE inference acceleration
